facts.what_happened: In 1999, first year as an RN at Grady.
Speaker states her age as twenty-two, already had Jaylen.
Speaker was placed on nights in the trauma side despite being a new grad because staff were short.
A Black woman, approximately thirty-five, came in reporting stomach pain.
Triage placed the woman in the hallway on a stretcher.
Speaker observed the woman was gray around the mouth.
Patient's blood pressure was about 98/60.
Patient's heart rate rose across checks: 106, 112, 118.
Speaker went to the resident, Dr. Kessler.
Speaker told Kessler the patient's rate was climbing and something was going on.
Kessler responded without looking up, stating the patient was anxious.
Kessler told her to go sit down because she looked tired.
Speaker sat down.
She sat for about ninety seconds.
She obtained a beta HCG test without an order, under a standing protocol she states did not technically apply.
She got ultrasound tech Clarence, who owed her for covering his lateness three times that month.
Clarence performed the ultrasound; the abdomen showed free fluid.
Diagnosis: ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
Speaker placed two large bore IVs, one in each AC.
Type and cross ordered/done.
Speaker called the OR directly rather than going through the resident.
Head of the bed was lowered.
Speaker talked through the situation with Nicole, who was orienting with her.
Patient taken to OR at approximately 0347; she survived.
Kessler said nothing to her afterward.
Kessler began reading her charting carefully after the event.
After her shift, speaker drove home; her mother had Jaylen, who had been up half the night with his ear.
Speaker sat in the driveway on Hollywood Road for about fifteen minutes.
She then went inside, did childcare tasks, slept two hours, and returned to work.

Speaker was working nights at Grady when EMS called in four patients from one scene, gunshot wounds
The incident occurred at an apartment complex off Cleveland Ave
In trauma, when there are multiple patients, the charge nurse assigns staff to patients
Speaker was not yet charge nurse; had four to five years of experience at the time

Bay two contained an eighteen-year-old with a chest wound and a blood pressure of seventy over palp
Speaker asked for patient two, saying "give me two"

Ghaffari asked the attending, "Is she the one calling it?"
The patient was taken to CT

The patient's pulse was restored for approximately nine minutes, then he died
The patient was eighteen years old
The patient's mother arrived wearing her work polo
Speaker gathered the newer staff after the event and led a step-by-step walkthrough of what happened
One of the staff members began crying during the walkthrough; speaker told her they would finish the walkthrough first
The walkthrough was completed, then the staff member cried
Speaker went home; Marcus's belongings were mostly moved out; Jaylen was at speaker's mother's house; Kiana was an infant still in a crib
